title: The Man and the Serpent

full_text:
A country farmer had an old serpent living beneath his doorstep, which in a moment of fury bit his beloved son, killing the boy instantly. Overwhelmed by grief and rage, the farmer seized an axe, chased the serpent, and struck at its head; but the blow missed, merely severing the serpent's tail and leaving a deep gash in the rock.

Later, realizing that perpetual hatred brought no peace, the farmer placed bread and milk before the hole, seeking reconciliation.

The serpent poked its head out, gazed at the offered meal, and hissed sorrowfully:

"Farmer, take away your bread. There can never be true peace between us. So long as you look upon your child's grave, and so long as I look upon my severed tail and the deep scar in that rock, the memory of our injuries will poison every handshake."
moral: True reconciliation is impossible where monuments of mutual injury remain.
